lines: Don't leave me in the Deep Dark. I do not want to learn what <pulse>hears me first</pulse> down there.
The Deep Dark is not a place for patience. It is a place for <shake>panic whispered quietly</shake>.
I stood in the Deep Dark afraid even my <pulse>breathing</pulse> was too loud once you were gone.
If you disappear in the Deep Dark, I am left measuring every sound like it might be my last.
Every step down there felt like a mistake waiting to be noticed.
I kept still for so long that even my own heartbeat felt dangerous.
Please do not leave me somewhere silence feels alive.
The Deep Dark made darkness feel heavy enough to press on my chest.
I was afraid to move, afraid to speak, and even more afraid to stay alone.
Down there, being left behind does not feel careless. It feels like a sentence.
Don't leave me in the Dripstone Caves. One wrong step and the cave does the rest.
The Dripstone Caves are all sharp ceilings and sharper floors. I hated waiting there alone.
I was stuck in the Dripstone Caves watching every spike like it had chosen me <italic>personally</italic>.
If you vanish in the Dripstone Caves, I am left between falling stone and bad footing.
Every drip sounded louder once I realized I was alone.
I kept looking up, then down, then up again. None of it helped.
Please do not leave me somewhere the cave has teeth on both sides.
The stone points made every path look like a warning.
I could not relax with sharp rock above me and sharper rock below.
I was standing in a cave that looked ready to punish the first bad step.
Don't leave me in the Lush Caves. Pretty moss does not make caves any safer.
The Lush Caves are beautiful until you remember how easy it is to get lost underground.
I was waiting in the Lush Caves with dripping water and too many unseen corners.
If you vanish in the Lush Caves, I am left admiring plants while worrying about monsters.
The glow berries helped me see just enough to know how much I could not see.
I kept hearing water, leaves, and every sound that might have been footsteps.
Please do not leave me somewhere beautiful enough to distract from the danger.
The moss softened the cave, but it did not make me feel safe.
Every opening looked like it could lead deeper, and deeper was not where I wanted to be.
I was alone underground, surrounded by green light and too many places for trouble to hide.
